name_or_item: NER Class EF1 (Shildon-Newport) - electrical parts only

notes: USD 19,500 per locomotive, about GBP 4,010 at USD 4.86 = GBP 1. Electrical equipment only; mechanical parts built at Darlington Works. The Electric Railway Journal (1 July 1916) names Siemens Brothers' Dynamo Works, Stafford, as the equipment installer. Total machine price is not stated.

name_or_item: LSWR 3-car electric units E1-E84 (conversion of steam stock)
scope: batch: 252 cars in 84 three-car units; about GBP 1,520 per car
source_ref: BloodandCustard, 'LSWR 3 Car Motor Units (3s)' page, section 'Units nos. E1-E84 (LSWR) Conversion to Electric Stock'
notes: Final reported cost of converting the rolling stock. Bodies converted at Eastleigh from LSWR bogie-block steam coaches built 1902-1912; traction equipment British Westinghouse (Trafford Park) under a March 1913 contract, installed by their own staff at Eastleigh. The LSWR estimated new construction would have cost about GBP 56,000 more. Derived: GBP 4,560 per three-car unit, about GBP 24-26 per seat at 178-190 seats. Confidence medium-low: detailed specialist site, but no document cited for the figure.
